tagline: Quartzite ridges and an iron furnace mark the Sauratown country
intro: North Carolina 89 connects Mount Airy with Westfield and Danbury, the county seat beside the Dan River. The Sauratown Mountains rise sharply above the surrounding country, with forested ridges broken by quartzite cliffs. NCDOT includes the Sauratown Mountains Scenic Byway in its Piedmont routes.

These peaks became parkland through separate efforts. In 1936, the Winston-Salem Foundation and Stokes County Committee for Hanging Rock donated land for a state park after a resort project failed. Pilot Mountain followed in 1968, protected from overdevelopment after a preservation committee raised money and obtained a federal grant to purchase the land.

From Mount Airy, N.C. 89 runs east through Westfield toward Danbury. Danbury stands on the Dan River near the entrance to Hanging Rock State Park. West of Danbury lies Moores Springs, also near Hanging Rock. Pilot Mountain State Park occupies the western end of the Sauratown range.

moments.title: Moratock Iron Furnace
moments.text: Moratock Iron Furnace survives in Danbury’s Moratock Park, where iron ore was once smelted. During the Civil War, Danbury supported the Confederate Army, though no battles occurred in the town. Union cavalry under George Stoneman destroyed most of the foundryworks during raids in 1865. The raid passed through Danbury on April 9, the day Confederate forces surrendered at Appomattox Court House. The furnace site is now part of a public park.

moments.title: Hanging Rock State Park
moments.text: Hanging Rock is one of the quartzite remnants left after erosion wore away surrounding rock. The Sauratown peaks stand apart from the Blue Ridge Mountains. A proposed resort on the highest summit failed when its developers went bankrupt. In 1936, the Winston-Salem Foundation and Stokes County Committee for Hanging Rock donated 3,096 acres to establish the park. The Civilian Conservation Corps built a dam, a 12-acre lake, trails and picnic and camping areas. The original facilities included a bathhouse, which entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1991.

moments.title: Pilot Mountain
moments.text: Big Pinnacle has bare rock walls beneath a rounded, vegetation-covered top. Its quartzite core resisted erosion while the surrounding mountain wore away. The Saura knew the mountain as Jomeokee, meaning the Great Guide; European settlers also used it as a guidepost and named it Pilot. After operating as a commercial tourist attraction, the mountain became a state park in 1968. Catawba rhododendron grows in a ring at Big Pinnacle and flowers pink in spring. Beside Big Pinnacle is Little Pinnacle, separated from the rounded knob by a curved depression that helps give the mountain its shape.
moments.notice: Big Pinnacle’s bare walls rise to a rounded top covered with vegetation.
